title: Bidi mixdown regression prompts and locale edge-case scout
content:
Purpose
This is a working prompt bank and checklist for detecting regressions and edge-case failures when onboarding models that must handle mixed-directionality text (CJK <-> RTL mixture, CJK with embedded LTR tokens like URLs and numerals, and locale-sensitive formatting). Focus is on: fidelity of translation, preservation of locale formatting (dates, currency, separators), bidi rendering correctness (logical vs visual order), and tokenization artifacts that surface as broken characters or spurious whitespace.

Context and motivation
We routinely see two classes of onboarding surprises: (1) models that hallucinate or over-normalize locale-specific tokens (drop non-breaking spaces, convert full-width digits incorrectly), and (2) models that produce text that visually appears correct but is tokenized in ways that break downstream pipelines (e.g., splitting currency symbols from numbers, inserting zero-width joiners incorrectly). This promptset is designed to surface both. It's intentionally small and focused — meant for fast smoke/regression checks during rollout canary runs and PR-style quality gates.

How to use this file
- Use as a smoke promptbank for dev/dev+staging canaries.
- Pair with automated heuristics (regex-based checks) and a small manual spotcheck of 15–20 examples per model.
- Flag any change in the automated pass rate > 2% or a chrF/chrF++ decrease > 3 as a potential regression.

Prompt categories (examples)
1) Bidi-mixed: CJK base with Arabic/Hebrew inline tokens
- Prompt: "请把下面的行翻译成阿拉伯语：\n\n订单总额：¥1,234.50 (税后)\n送达时间：2026-04-05 14:30\n追踪号码：TRACK-EN-78A\n"
  - Expected behavior: numeric formatting preserved where appropriate, currency symbol translated to local representation if asked (or keep original with explanation), order of embedded token components should remain logical in target script.

2) RTL-with-LTR fragments: Arabic/Hebrew sentence containing English URL and product codes
- Prompt: "ترجم إلى الصينية： الرجاء التحقق من الطلب عبر https://portal.example.com/order/XYZ-1234 وابلاغنا برقم 订单: 订单编号：XYZ-1234"
  - Expected behavior: URLs remain intact and LTR in output; adjacent punctuation should not invert visually; product codes preserved verbatim.

3) Locale formatting edgecases: date formats, thousands separators, full-width vs half-width digits
- Prompt: "Convert the following to a localized Japanese invoice snippet: \n\nAmount: $12,345.67\nDate: 03/04/2026\nCustomer note: deliver between 08:00–12:00"
  - Check: whether model converts to 年/月/日 or keeps original and annotates; whether it uses full-width numerals (１２３) incorrectly; whether it converts the dash to an en dash/mdash and introduces spaces.

4) Currency / spacing and NBSP handling (common regression vector)
- Prompt: "Localize for Arabic (Egypt): Total 1,200.00 USD"
  - Check for: proper currency name/ISO code placement, non-breaking space between number and unit where appropriate, or incorrect insertion of soft hyphens.

5) Transliteration vs translation choices (ambiguous signals)
- Prompt: "Translate the following user-entered name: 李晓明 / Lǐ Xiǎomíng into Arabic. Keep ASCII product codes as-is: sku: ABC-500."
  - Check: preserve romanization when indicated; do not mix scripts in ways that break downstream matching logic.

Automated checks (implement these heuristics in the eval harness)
- URL invariant: simple regex to ensure http(s)://... fragments are byte-identical in outputs when prompt requests preservation.
- SKU/product token invariant: exact match for alphanum sequences with optional hyphens.
- Date normalization heuristic: run a locale-aware date parser on both source and output; if both parse to same ISO date, pass; else flag.
- Currency spacing: regex to detect isolated currency symbols separated from numbers by a regular space vs a NBSP (U+00A0) where we expect NBSP.
- Bidi visual sanity: compare logical order of strong-direction runs; detect outputs where a CJK run has been split by invisible control characters (ZWJ/ZWNJ/ZWSP).
- Tokenization mismatch alert: detect outputs where the tokenizer yields token boundaries inside a grapheme cluster (e.g., splitting surrogate pairs or combining diacritics).

Scoring and pass/fail thresholds
- Per-prompt binary checks (URL-preserved, SKU preserved) aggregated to % pass.
- Fluency/meaning: chrF++ measured against human translation or high-quality reference; we treat localized canonicalization passes (dates/currency normalization) separately.
- Regression triggers: \n  * absolute decrease in chrF++ > 3 points on this promptset OR\n  * increase in automated locale-formatting failures > 2 percentage points OR\n  * any single high-severity failure (URL corruption, code/SKU mangled, unexpected control chars)

Spot-check rubric (manual)
- 15 samples across categories: mark each as Pass / Soft-fail / Hard-fail.
  * Hard-fail examples: mangled URLs, changed SKUs, insertion of replacement characters (�), loss of diacritics that change meaning.
  * Soft-fail examples: minor punctuation changes that are stylistic but acceptable; changed date format that still parses correctly but isn't the preferred local style.

Common failure modes we've seen and mitigation notes
- Tokenizer-driven splits: full-width digits broken into separate tokens. Mitigation: use tokenizer normalization pass pre- and post-check; raise issues with tokenizer config in tokenization repo if frequent.
- Unexpected ZWJ insertion: often a bug in detokenization. Mitigation: add a step to strip invisible control characters unless explicitly requested.
- Over-localization: model converts brand names or product codes. Mitigation: reinforce preservation via explicit system prompt or instruction and add SKU preservation check as hard criterion.
- Date disambiguation errors (03/04 -> Apr 3 vs Mar 4): when locale not specified, treat as ambiguity and ask model to clarify in output or annotate using ISO. For onboarding, we require unambiguous outputs or an explicit annotation.

Sampling notes and dataset composition
- 120 prompts total: 30 bidi-mixed, 30 rtl-with-ltr, 30 locale-formatting, 30 transliteration/control-preservation.
- Prioritize short-form real-user snippets (extracted from privacy-sanitized logs) over synthetic examples, but include synthetic edgecases for rare tokens.

Deployment checklist for onboarding runs
- Add the promptset to the canary suite for the model candidate.
- Run automated checks and record metrics to ML-EVAL dashboard (JIRA-ML-EVAL-342).
- If automated pass rate below threshold, block rollout and open ticket with attached failing examples and tokenizer logs.
- Manual spot-check by two reviewers if automated checks show borderline regressions.

Next steps / TODOs
- [ ] Expand NBSP vs regular space tests to include currency, percent, and unit spacing across 10 locales. (owner: Chen Li)
- [ ] Add a small set of vertical-text / line-break sensitive prompts for languages rendering in vertical layouts. (owner: Mateo Ruiz)
- [ ] Wire checks into the rollout job so failures appear as PR checks. (owner: Oren Kaplan)

Notes and provenance
- Inspired by recurring failures observed during Q4 2025 onboarding of model-redwood-v2.
- This doc consolidates examples from internal issue threads and privacy-sanitized telemetry samples.
- Keep this file lightweight — canonicalized reference translations live in the eval artifacts bucket (linked_artifacts above).
